newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's PM says army no threat to democracy.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's PM says army no threat to democracy.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday that the armed forces, which are increasingly at odds with his Islamist government, posed no threat to democracy.
"The army is completely loyal to democracy," Erbakan told parliamentary deputies from his Islam-based Welfare Party. "Let no one make use of the army for their own purposes."
Turkey's armed forces, traditional defenders of the secularist system, have brought down three civilian government since 1960.
Referring to rumours of a fourth military coup, Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, said: "It's all lies, it's all hollow, it's all empty."

A row between the Islamists and the military over religious activism threatens to topple Erbakan's 10-month-old coalition and opposition leaders have begun a search for a new "Islamist-free" government formula.
However, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller has so far stood by Erbakan, whose party has made clear it is not prepared to go along with some military demands for a crackdown on a religious revival.
